# First-run onboarding wizard (issue #151)

## Context

Issue [#151](https://github.com/joelmoss/workroom/issues/151): "Need a great looking startup intro
and flow for first time usage." The issue body is a single sentence with no further spec.

Research confirms nothing like this exists today: no first-run flag, no welcome window. A brand-new
install currently just shows `ProjectSidebar`'s empty-project `ContentUnavailableView` with an "Add
Project…" button — functional, not an "intro."

Scope was narrowed with the user via Q&A:
- A **4-step wizard** (Welcome → Feature tour → Add Project → Done), not a single sheet.
- Triggers on **first launch ever, only while zero projects are registered** — one-shot, but if
  closed before finishing, it shows again next launch.
- Presented in a **dedicated onboarding window** (its own SwiftUI `Scene`, like `Settings`), not a
  sheet over the main window.
- The existing `ProjectSidebar` empty state stays untouched as the fallback for anyone who
  dismisses/skips the wizard early.

## Design decisions from verified research

- **Reuse, don't rebuild, the Add Project *logic*.** `AddProjectSheetModel` (path validation,
  normalization, footer text — `Views/AddProjectSheet.swift:16-54`) is already pure and tested
  (`AddProjectSheetModelTests.swift`). Reuse it directly. But `AddProjectSheet` the *view* is a
  self-contained dialog with its own header (icon + "New Project" title) and its own Cancel/Add
  footer, sized `.frame(width: 460)` — embedding it verbatim inside the wizard's 560×480 canvas
  would visually read as a dialog nested inside a dialog (its own header on top of the wizard's step
  header, its own button row on top of the wizard's Back/Next footer), which fails the issue's own
  "great looking" bar on the one step users actually interact with. Fix: extract the middle of
  `AddProjectSheet` — the `Picker("Source")` + path `TextField` + "Choose…" button + footer caption —
  into a small reusable `AddProjectFields` view (`@Binding mode`, `@Binding path`, `@Binding
  showChooser`, same `.fileImporter`). `AddProjectSheet` keeps its existing header/Cancel/Add
  wrapper around `AddProjectFields` (unchanged behavior, unchanged tests, unchanged call sites
  elsewhere in the app). The wizard's Add-Project step wraps the same `AddProjectFields` in its own
  step header and wires Add/Skip into the wizard's own footer buttons instead of `AddProjectSheet`'s —
  one shared, tested core; two different, consistently-chromed shells.
- **Success/failure signal**: verified `AppStore.addProject(_:create:)` (`Core/AppStore.swift:2983-
  2999`) has no return value — on failure it calls `present(_:)` (line 4569-4572), which sets
  `errorMessage`, the same field `RootView`'s `.alert` binds to for every other error on that window
  (`RootView.swift:174-192`, cleared to `nil` on dismiss). A bare `Bool` return (an earlier draft of
  this plan) would discard the actual error and leave the wizard looking unresponsive on failure
  while the real explanation surfaces as an alert on the main window, possibly hidden behind the
  onboarding window — caught by this review's outside-voice pass. Fix: `addProject` returns
  `Result<Void, Error>` (or throws) instead of `Bool`. It still unconditionally calls `present(error)`
  internally on failure first — so the existing sidebar/`AddProjectSheet` call site's behavior is
  byte-for-byte unchanged — and then also surfaces the error to its caller. The wizard's `handleAdd`
  reads the `Result` and shows the error text **inline in the Add-Project step itself** on failure,
  rather than relying on the (possibly-hidden) main-window alert. Both can legitimately fire for the
  same failure (main-window alert + wizard-inline text) — harmless duplication, not a bug: the
  wizard's copy of the state doesn't touch `store.errorMessage` itself, it just also renders the same
  underlying error locally.
- **Drive the real launch-window store, not a throwaway one.** `AppStore.addProject(_:create:)`
  (`Core/AppStore.swift:2983-2999`) does more than register a path — after `reload()` it selects the
  new project (issue #104). A throwaway `AppStore` built just for the onboarding window would apply
  that selection to a store nobody's looking at, leaving the real window's sidebar showing the new
  project with nothing selected. Fix: the wizard's Add-Project step calls
  `WindowRegistry.shared.lastActiveStore?.addProject(...)` — by construction the launch `RootWindow`
  is already registered (and thus `lastActiveStore` non-nil) before the wizard's `.task` can open it.
- **No new `WindowRegistry` registration for the onboarding window.** Leaving it unregistered is what
  makes every existing aux-window carve-out (⌘W fallback, shortcut/switcher no-ops, quit/window-count
  logic, ⌘\` cycle exclusion) apply for free — verified these all key off `WindowRegistry.store(for:)
  == nil`, exactly like Settings/About today. No new code needed in any of those paths.
- **Theming**: read `ThemeService.shared.tokens.*` directly (the actual pattern `WhatsNewSheet`/
  `SettingsView` use — not `@Environment`, despite a stray doc comment suggesting otherwise).
- **No new pager dependency.** No `TabView(.page…)`/carousel exists anywhere in the app; `.page`
  style is iOS-primary anyway. A plain step-`switch` + a small dot-indicator `HStack` is enough for a
  fixed 4-step linear flow.
- **The Window-menu item is kept only until onboarding completes.** A SwiftUI `Window` scene
  auto-adds "Welcome to Workroom" to the app's Window menu. Since the window is a plain (non-modal,
  unattached) window, it can be clicked behind the main window with no other way back — so the menu
  item is a real recovery path *while onboarding is still incomplete*. But this review's outside-voice
  pass caught that the original draft left it reachable forever, meaning a user who already completed
  onboarding could reopen the full first-run flow — including a working Add Project step — from an
  arbitrary window, with no defined behavior for that case. Fix: suppress the menu item once
  `Defaults[.hasCompletedOnboarding]` is `true`. Sketch: give `WorkroomApp` a
  `@Default(.hasCompletedOnboarding) private var hasCompletedOnboarding` and branch the `Window`
  scene in an `if`/`else` inside the `body`'s `SceneBuilder` (conditional `Scene` branches are valid
  `SceneBuilder` syntax) — completed branch applies `.commandsRemoved()` to drop the scene's own
  Window-menu contribution while keeping the scene declared (so a still-in-progress session that
  completes mid-run doesn't need the app relaunched for the item to disappear next time). **Verify at
  implementation time**: confirm `.commandsRemoved()` on a `Window` scene strips only its Window-menu
  entry and not the scene's ability to be opened via `openWindow(id:)` — this is inferred from how
  `.commandsRemoved()` behaves on `Settings`, not independently confirmed for `Window`.
- **A plain `Window` scene is resizable by default; a fixed content `.frame()` alone doesn't stop
  that.** The original draft compared this to `SettingsView`'s fixed frame as precedent for a
  non-resizable window — wrong comparison, caught by the outside-voice pass: `Settings`' own
  non-resizability comes from the `Settings` scene type itself, not from its content's `.frame()`.
  Fix: add `.windowResizability(.contentSize)` to the `Window` scene declaration (documented SwiftUI
  API, macOS 13+).
- **Window resizability/isRestorable have no automated test, matching existing precedent.** Both are
  either hard to exercise in XCUITest (dragging window edges) or actively defeated by
  `-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES`, which most of this suite's launches pass to suppress the "restore
  previous session" dialog. This isn't a new gap — the main window's own `isRestorable = false`
  (`AppStore.swift:1104`) has no dedicated automated test either. Verified manually only (see
  Verification).
- **Existing user with zero projects at upgrade time sees onboarding once — accepted, not fixed.**
  The gate (`!hasCompleted && projectsEmpty`) can't distinguish a genuinely fresh install from an
  existing user who currently has no projects registered (e.g. deleted their only one). That user
  sees the wizard once after upgrading to the version shipping #151, even though it isn't their first
  launch. Accepted as a narrow, one-time, self-correcting cosmetic caveat (the flag flips true the
  moment they see it or add a project) rather than building install-vs-upgrade migration detection for
  it.
- **Add-Project step's form state is lifted into `OnboardingWindow`, not owned by the step.** The
  wizard's shared footer needs to read the step's path/mode validity to enable its own Add button —
  caught by the outside-voice pass as unaddressed in the original draft, which gave `OnboardingWindow`
  only a `step` `@State` with the form state implicitly (and unworkably) trapped inside a child view.
  Fix: `@State private var addProjectMode: AddProjectMode = .existing` and `@State private var
  addProjectPath: String = ""` live on `OnboardingWindow` itself, passed down as `@Binding`s into
  `AddProjectFields`; the footer reads `AddProjectSheetModel.isValid(mode:path:)` directly off that
  same parent-owned state.
- **In-flight guard on the Add-Project step.** `handleAdd` is `async`; nothing stopped a double-click
  or a Back/Skip click mid-request. Fix: `@State private var isAdding = false` on `OnboardingWindow`,
  set before calling `addProject`, gating Add/Back/Skip disabled while `true`, with a small progress
  indicator.
- **Completion flag is set on entering `.done`, not only on exiting it via "Get Started."** The
  original draft only wrote `Defaults[.hasCompletedOnboarding] = true` inside `finish()` (bound to the
  Get Started button) and inside a successful `handleAdd`. Caught by the outside-voice pass: a user
  who reaches Done and then closes the window some other way (⌘W, red button) instead of clicking Get
  Started would see "you're all set" but the flag would stay `false`, reopening the wizard next
  launch despite the user visibly having finished. Fix: set the flag the moment `step` becomes
  `.done` (e.g. `.onChange(of: step) { if step == .done { Defaults[.hasCompletedOnboarding] = true } }`),

### 1. New Defaults key — `Core/DefaultsKeys.swift`

Add next to `lastSeenVersion` (same "unset = first launch" shape):

```swift
/// Whether the first-launch onboarding wizard (issue #151) has been completed. Unset (false) on a
/// fresh install. Flips true the moment the wizard reaches its "Done" step, by any path (skip or a
/// successful add) — not gated behind which button the user then uses to close the window. The
/// show-gate (`OnboardingGate.shouldShow`) also checks `projects.isEmpty`, so a project added some
/// other way suppresses the wizard too — this flag only needs writing from the wizard itself, not
/// from `AppStore.addProject`'s general path.
static let hasCompletedOnboarding = Key<Bool>("onboarding.hasCompleted", default: false)
```

  step view is shown.
- `enum OnboardingGate { static func shouldShow(hasCompleted: Bool, projectsEmpty: Bool, override:
  Bool? = UITestFixture.onboardingOverride) -> Bool }` — pure, unit-testable (mirrors
  `AddProjectSheetModel`'s "pure logic beside its view" pattern). `!hasCompleted && projectsEmpty`,
  with `override` short-circuiting for UI tests.

  tour step, copy grounded in the app's real shipped features (workrooms via Git worktrees/JJ
  workspaces, the embedded terminal, the unified project sidebar, run-command supervision).
- `struct OnboardingWindow: View` — the Scene's root view:
  - `@State private var step: OnboardingStep = .welcome`, `@Environment(\.dismissWindow)`.
  - Add-Project form state lives here, not in the step view (see design decisions — the footer needs
    it): `@State private var addProjectMode: AddProjectMode = .existing`, `@State private var
    addProjectPath: String = ""`, `@State private var showChooser = false`, `@State private var
    isAdding = false`, `@State private var addProjectError: String?`.
  - `body`: `VStack { content; Divider(); footer }.frame(width: 560, height: 480)` — the fixed frame
    alone does NOT make the window non-resizable (see design decisions); `.windowResizability(.contentSize)`
    on the `Window` scene declaration (§3) is what does that.
  - `content`: switches on `step` — `.welcome`/`.tour` are new small step views; `.addProject` is a
    new `OnboardingAddProjectStep` wrapping the shared `AddProjectFields` (bound to the parent's
    `addProjectMode`/`addProjectPath`/`showChooser`), showing `addProjectError` inline when non-nil,
    with its own step header; `.done` is a "You're all set" screen with a "Get Started" button.
  - `footer`: Back (steps after `.tour`), step-dot indicator, Next (on `.welcome`/`.tour`), Add
    Project/Skip (on `.addProject`, replacing Next — Add disabled while `isAdding` or
    `!AddProjectSheetModel.isValid(mode: addProjectMode, path: addProjectPath)`; Back/Skip also
    disabled while `isAdding`).
  - `.onChange(of: step) { if step == .done { Defaults[.hasCompletedOnboarding] = true } }` — the
    ONE place the completion flag is set, firing on entry to Done by any path (skip or successful
    add), not gated behind which button later closes the window (see design decisions).
  - `handleAdd(_:create:)`: sets `isAdding = true`; resolves `WindowRegistry.shared.lastActiveStore`;
    calls the now-`Result`-returning `store.addProject(path, create: create)` — on `.success`,
    advance to `.done` (which fires the `.onChange` above); on `.failure(let error)`, set
    `addProjectError` to the error's text and leave the step up so the user can retry. Clears
    `isAdding` in both cases.
  - "Get Started" on the Done step just calls `dismissWindow(id: OnboardingWindow.sceneID)` — the
    flag is already set by the `.onChange` above, not by this button.
  - No `WindowRegistry.register`/`store.attachWindow` call anywhere in this view — that omission is
    the load-bearing part of the aux-window integration (see design decisions above). It DOES still
    need one `WindowAccessor { $0.isRestorable = false }` (no store/registry involved) — verified via
    a prior cross-session learning that `AppStore.swift:1104` sets this specifically to stop macOS's
    own Cocoa window-state restoration from reopening a window independently of the app's own
    session/gate logic, and that this dev machine has the gating pref
    (`NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows`) on. Without it, quitting with the wizard open could have macOS
    silently reopen it on next launch in parallel with `OnboardingGate`'s own re-open check.

### 3. Scene wiring — `WorkroomApp.swift`

Add a `Window` scene (macOS 13+, fine at this app's macOS 15+ floor) in `WorkroomApp.body`, alongside
`Settings`. Conditioned on completion (see design decisions — the Window-menu item should disappear
once onboarding is done) via a `@Default` read on `WorkroomApp` itself and a conditional `SceneBuilder`
branch:

```swift
@Default(.hasCompletedOnboarding) private var hasCompletedOnboarding  // on WorkroomApp

// in body:
if hasCompletedOnboarding {
  Window("Welcome to Workroom", id: OnboardingWindow.sceneID) { OnboardingWindow() }
    .windowResizability(.contentSize)
    .commandsRemoved()  // drop the Window-menu entry; verify this doesn't also block openWindow(id:)
} else {
  Window("Welcome to Workroom", id: OnboardingWindow.sceneID) { OnboardingWindow() }
    .windowResizability(.contentSize)
}
```

In `RootWindow.body`'s existing `.task` (`WorkroomApp.swift:155-174`), right after `await
store.bootstrap(restore: seed.restore)` and the `guard seed.isLaunch else { return }`, before the
session-restore fan-out loop:

```swift

  hasCompleted: Defaults[.hasCompletedOnboarding], projectsEmpty: store.projects.isEmpty
) {
  openWindow(id: OnboardingWindow.sceneID)
}
```

Uses the `@Environment(\.openWindow)` already declared on `RootWindow` (`WorkroomApp.swift:122`).
Gating on `seed.isLaunch` (already required to reach this point in the `.task`) is exactly what stops
onboarding from being reconsidered on a ⌘N window — only the launch window's `.task` body reaches
this line at all.

Extracted as a testable static helper rather than left inline (the `.task` closure body itself isn't
unit-testable, and it's the one seam in this feature with no test at all otherwise):

```swift
extension RootWindow {
  static func shouldOpenOnboarding(seed: WindowSeed, hasCompleted: Bool, projectsEmpty: Bool) -> Bool {
    seed.isLaunch && OnboardingGate.shouldShow(hasCompleted: hasCompleted, projectsEmpty: projectsEmpty)

}
```

The `.task` body calls this instead of duplicating the `seed.isLaunch &&` check.

Issue [#151](https://github.com/joelmoss/workroom/issues/151): "Need a great looking startup intro
and flow for first time usage." The issue body is a single sentence with no further spec.

Research confirms nothing like this exists today: no first-run flag, no welcome window. A brand-new
install currently just shows `ProjectSidebar`'s empty-project `ContentUnavailableView` with an "Add
Project…" button — functional, not an "intro."

Scope was narrowed with the user via Q&A:
- A **4-step wizard** (Welcome → Feature tour → Add Project → Done), not a single sheet.
- Triggers on **first launch ever, only while zero projects are registered** — one-shot, but if
  closed before finishing, it shows again next launch.
- Presented in a **dedicated onboarding window** (its own SwiftUI `Scene`, like `Settings`), not a
  sheet over the main window.
- The existing `ProjectSidebar` empty state stays untouched as the fallback for anyone who
  dismisses/skips the wizard early.

## Design decisions from verified research

- **Reuse, don't rebuild, the Add Project *logic*.** `AddProjectSheetModel` (path validation,
  normalization, footer text — `Views/AddProjectSheet.swift:16-54`) is already pure and tested
  (`AddProjectSheetModelTests.swift`). Reuse it directly. But `AddProjectSheet` the *view* is a
  self-contained dialog with its own header (icon + "New Project" title) and its own Cancel/Add
  footer, sized `.frame(width: 460)` — embedding it verbatim inside the wizard's 560×480 canvas
  would visually read as a dialog nested inside a dialog (its own header on top of the wizard's step
  header, its own button row on top of the wizard's Back/Next footer), which fails the issue's own
  "great looking" bar on the one step users actually interact with. Fix: extract the middle of
  `AddProjectSheet` — the `Picker("Source")` + path `TextField` + "Choose…" button + footer caption —
  into a small reusable `AddProjectFields` view (`@Binding mode`, `@Binding path`, `@Binding
  showChooser`, same `.fileImporter`). `AddProjectSheet` keeps its existing header/Cancel/Add
  wrapper around `AddProjectFields` (unchanged behavior, unchanged tests, unchanged call sites
  elsewhere in the app). The wizard's Add-Project step wraps the same `AddProjectFields` in its own
  step header and wires Add/Skip into the wizard's own footer buttons instead of `AddProjectSheet`'s —
  one shared, tested core; two different, consistently-chromed shells.
- **Success/failure signal**: verified `AppStore.addProject(_:create:)` (`Core/AppStore.swift:2983-
  2999`) has no return value — on failure it calls `present(_:)` (line 4569-4572), which sets
  `errorMessage`, the same field `RootView`'s `.alert` binds to for every other error on that window
  (`RootView.swift:174-192`, cleared to `nil` on dismiss). A bare `Bool` return (an earlier draft of
  this plan) would discard the actual error and leave the wizard looking unresponsive on failure
  while the real explanation surfaces as an alert on the main window, possibly hidden behind the
  onboarding window — caught by this review's outside-voice pass. Fix: `addProject` returns
  `Result<Void, Error>` (or throws) instead of `Bool`. It still unconditionally calls `present(error)`
  internally on failure first — so the existing sidebar/`AddProjectSheet` call site's behavior is
  byte-for-byte unchanged — and then also surfaces the error to its caller. The wizard's `handleAdd`
  reads the `Result` and shows the error text **inline in the Add-Project step itself** on failure,
  rather than relying on the (possibly-hidden) main-window alert. Both can legitimately fire for the
  same failure (main-window alert + wizard-inline text) — harmless duplication, not a bug: the
  wizard's copy of the state doesn't touch `store.errorMessage` itself, it just also renders the same
  underlying error locally.
- **Drive the real launch-window store, not a throwaway one.** `AppStore.addProject(_:create:)`
  (`Core/AppStore.swift:2983-2999`) does more than register a path — after `reload()` it selects the
  new project (issue #104). A throwaway `AppStore` built just for the onboarding window would apply
  that selection to a store nobody's looking at, leaving the real window's sidebar showing the new
  project with nothing selected. Fix: the wizard's Add-Project step calls
  `WindowRegistry.shared.lastActiveStore?.addProject(...)` — by construction the launch `RootWindow`
  is already registered (and thus `lastActiveStore` non-nil) before the wizard's `.task` can open it.
- **No new `WindowRegistry` registration for the onboarding window.** Leaving it unregistered is what
  makes every existing aux-window carve-out (⌘W fallback, shortcut/switcher no-ops, quit/window-count
  logic, ⌘\` cycle exclusion) apply for free — verified these all key off `WindowRegistry.store(for:)
  == nil`, exactly like Settings/About today. No new code needed in any of those paths.
- **Theming**: read `ThemeService.shared.tokens.*` directly (the actual pattern `WhatsNewSheet`/
  `SettingsView` use — not `@Environment`, despite a stray doc comment suggesting otherwise).
- **No new pager dependency.** No `TabView(.page…)`/carousel exists anywhere in the app; `.page`
  style is iOS-primary anyway. A plain step-`switch` + a small dot-indicator `HStack` is enough for a
  fixed 4-step linear flow.
- **The Window-menu item is kept only until onboarding completes.** A SwiftUI `Window` scene
  auto-adds "Welcome to Workroom" to the app's Window menu. Since the window is a plain (non-modal,
  unattached) window, it can be clicked behind the main window with no other way back — so the menu
  item is a real recovery path *while onboarding is still incomplete*. But this review's outside-voice
  pass caught that the original draft left it reachable forever, meaning a user who already completed
  onboarding could reopen the full first-run flow — including a working Add Project step — from an
  arbitrary window, with no defined behavior for that case. Fix: suppress the menu item once
  `Defaults[.hasCompletedOnboarding]` is `true`. Sketch: give `WorkroomApp` a
  `@Default(.hasCompletedOnboarding) private var hasCompletedOnboarding` and branch the `Window`
  scene in an `if`/`else` inside the `body`'s `SceneBuilder` (conditional `Scene` branches are valid
  `SceneBuilder` syntax) — completed branch applies `.commandsRemoved()` to drop the scene's own
  Window-menu contribution while keeping the scene declared (so a still-in-progress session that
  completes mid-run doesn't need the app relaunched for the item to disappear next time). **Verify at
  implementation time**: confirm `.commandsRemoved()` on a `Window` scene strips only its Window-menu
  entry and not the scene's ability to be opened via `openWindow(id:)` — this is inferred from how
  `.commandsRemoved()` behaves on `Settings`, not independently confirmed for `Window`.
- **A plain `Window` scene is resizable by default; a fixed content `.frame()` alone doesn't stop
  that.** The original draft compared this to `SettingsView`'s fixed frame as precedent for a
  non-resizable window — wrong comparison, caught by the outside-voice pass: `Settings`' own
  non-resizability comes from the `Settings` scene type itself, not from its content's `.frame()`.
  Fix: add `.windowResizability(.contentSize)` to the `Window` scene declaration (documented SwiftUI
  API, macOS 13+).
- **Window resizability/isRestorable have no automated test, matching existing precedent.** Both are
  either hard to exercise in XCUITest (dragging window edges) or actively defeated by
  `-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES`, which most of this suite's launches pass to suppress the "restore
  previous session" dialog. This isn't a new gap — the main window's own `isRestorable = false`
  (`AppStore.swift:1104`) has no dedicated automated test either. Verified manually only (see
  Verification).
- **Existing user with zero projects at upgrade time sees onboarding once — accepted, not fixed.**
  The gate (`!hasCompleted && projectsEmpty`) can't distinguish a genuinely fresh install from an
  existing user who currently has no projects registered (e.g. deleted their only one). That user
  sees the wizard once after upgrading to the version shipping #151, even though it isn't their first
  launch. Accepted as a narrow, one-time, self-correcting cosmetic caveat (the flag flips true the
  moment they see it or add a project) rather than building install-vs-upgrade migration detection for
  it.
- **Add-Project step's form state is lifted into `OnboardingWindow`, not owned by the step.** The
  wizard's shared footer needs to read the step's path/mode validity to enable its own Add button —
  caught by the outside-voice pass as unaddressed in the original draft, which gave `OnboardingWindow`
  only a `step` `@State` with the form state implicitly (and unworkably) trapped inside a child view.
  Fix: `@State private var addProjectMode: AddProjectMode = .existing` and `@State private var
  addProjectPath: String = ""` live on `OnboardingWindow` itself, passed down as `@Binding`s into
  `AddProjectFields`; the footer reads `AddProjectSheetModel.isValid(mode:path:)` directly off that
  same parent-owned state.
- **In-flight guard on the Add-Project step.** `handleAdd` is `async`; nothing stopped a double-click
  or a Back/Skip click mid-request. Fix: `@State private var isAdding = false` on `OnboardingWindow`,
  set before calling `addProject`, gating Add/Back/Skip disabled while `true`, with a small progress
  indicator.
- **Completion flag is set on entering `.done`, not only on exiting it via "Get Started."** The
  original draft only wrote `Defaults[.hasCompletedOnboarding] = true` inside `finish()` (bound to the
  Get Started button) and inside a successful `handleAdd`. Caught by the outside-voice pass: a user
  who reaches Done and then closes the window some other way (⌘W, red button) instead of clicking Get
  Started would see "you're all set" but the flag would stay `false`, reopening the wizard next
  launch despite the user visibly having finished. Fix: set the flag the moment `step` becomes
  `.done` (e.g. `.onChange(of: step) { if step == .done { Defaults[.hasCompletedOnboarding] = true } }`),
  regardless of which path led there or how the window is later closed.

## Implementation

### 1. New Defaults key — `Core/DefaultsKeys.swift`

Add next to `lastSeenVersion` (same "unset = first launch" shape):

```swift
/// Whether the first-launch onboarding wizard (issue #151) has been completed. Unset (false) on a
/// fresh install. Flips true the moment the wizard reaches its "Done" step, by any path (skip or a
/// successful add) — not gated behind which button the user then uses to close the window. The
/// show-gate (`OnboardingGate.shouldShow`) also checks `projects.isEmpty`, so a project added some
/// other way suppresses the wizard too — this flag only needs writing from the wizard itself, not
/// from `AppStore.addProject`'s general path.
static let hasCompletedOnboarding = Key<Bool>("onboarding.hasCompleted", default: false)
```

### 2. New file — `Views/OnboardingWindow.swift`

- `enum OnboardingStep: Int, CaseIterable { case welcome, tour, addProject, done }` — drives which
  step view is shown.
- `enum OnboardingGate { static func shouldShow(hasCompleted: Bool, projectsEmpty: Bool, override:
  Bool? = UITestFixture.onboardingOverride) -> Bool }` — pure, unit-testable (mirrors
  `AddProjectSheetModel`'s "pure logic beside its view" pattern). `!hasCompleted && projectsEmpty`,
  with `override` short-circuiting for UI tests.
- `struct OnboardingFeature: Identifiable` + `static let all: [OnboardingFeature]` — 3-4 cards for the
  tour step, copy grounded in the app's real shipped features (workrooms via Git worktrees/JJ
  workspaces, the embedded terminal, the unified project sidebar, run-command supervision).
- `struct OnboardingWindow: View` — the Scene's root view:
  - `@State private var step: OnboardingStep = .welcome`, `@Environment(\.dismissWindow)`.
  - Add-Project form state lives here, not in the step view (see design decisions — the footer needs
    it): `@State private var addProjectMode: AddProjectMode = .existing`, `@State private var
    addProjectPath: String = ""`, `@State private var showChooser = false`, `@State private var
    isAdding = false`, `@State private var addProjectError: String?`.
  - `body`: `VStack { content; Divider(); footer }.frame(width: 560, height: 480)` — the fixed frame
    alone does NOT make the window non-resizable (see design decisions); `.windowResizability(.contentSize)`
    on the `Window` scene declaration (§3) is what does that.
  - `content`: switches on `step` — `.welcome`/`.tour` are new small step views; `.addProject` is a
    new `OnboardingAddProjectStep` wrapping the shared `AddProjectFields` (bound to the parent's
    `addProjectMode`/`addProjectPath`/`showChooser`), showing `addProjectError` inline when non-nil,
    with its own step header; `.done` is a "You're all set" screen with a "Get Started" button.
  - `footer`: Back (steps after `.tour`), step-dot indicator, Next (on `.welcome`/`.tour`), Add
    Project/Skip (on `.addProject`, replacing Next — Add disabled while `isAdding` or
    `!AddProjectSheetModel.isValid(mode: addProjectMode, path: addProjectPath)`; Back/Skip also
    disabled while `isAdding`).
  - `.onChange(of: step) { if step == .done { Defaults[.hasCompletedOnboarding] = true } }` — the
    ONE place the completion flag is set, firing on entry to Done by any path (skip or successful
    add), not gated behind which button later closes the window (see design decisions).
  - `handleAdd(_:create:)`: sets `isAdding = true`; resolves `WindowRegistry.shared.lastActiveStore`;
    calls the now-`Result`-returning `store.addProject(path, create: create)` — on `.success`,
    advance to `.done` (which fires the `.onChange` above); on `.failure(let error)`, set
    `addProjectError` to the error's text and leave the step up so the user can retry. Clears
    `isAdding` in both cases.
  - "Get Started" on the Done step just calls `dismissWindow(id: OnboardingWindow.sceneID)` — the
    flag is already set by the `.onChange` above, not by this button.
  - No `WindowRegistry.register`/`store.attachWindow` call anywhere in this view — that omission is
    the load-bearing part of the aux-window integration (see design decisions above). It DOES still
    need one `WindowAccessor { $0.isRestorable = false }` (no store/registry involved) — verified via
    a prior cross-session learning that `AppStore.swift:1104` sets this specifically to stop macOS's
    own Cocoa window-state restoration from reopening a window independently of the app's own
    session/gate logic, and that this dev machine has the gating pref
    (`NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows`) on. Without it, quitting with the wizard open could have macOS
    silently reopen it on next launch in parallel with `OnboardingGate`'s own re-open check.

### 3. Scene wiring — `WorkroomApp.swift`

Add a `Window` scene (macOS 13+, fine at this app's macOS 15+ floor) in `WorkroomApp.body`, alongside
`Settings`. Conditioned on completion (see design decisions — the Window-menu item should disappear
once onboarding is done) via a `@Default` read on `WorkroomApp` itself and a conditional `SceneBuilder`
branch:

```swift
@Default(.hasCompletedOnboarding) private var hasCompletedOnboarding  // on WorkroomApp

// in body:
if hasCompletedOnboarding {
  Window("Welcome to Workroom", id: OnboardingWindow.sceneID) { OnboardingWindow() }
    .windowResizability(.contentSize)
    .commandsRemoved()  // drop the Window-menu entry; verify this doesn't also block openWindow(id:)
} else {
  Window("Welcome to Workroom", id: OnboardingWindow.sceneID) { OnboardingWindow() }
    .windowResizability(.contentSize)
}
```

In `RootWindow.body`'s existing `.task` (`WorkroomApp.swift:155-174`), right after `await
store.bootstrap(restore: seed.restore)` and the `guard seed.isLaunch else { return }`, before the
session-restore fan-out loop:

```swift
if OnboardingGate.shouldShow(
  hasCompleted: Defaults[.hasCompletedOnboarding], projectsEmpty: store.projects.isEmpty
) {
  openWindow(id: OnboardingWindow.sceneID)
}
```

Uses the `@Environment(\.openWindow)` already declared on `RootWindow` (`WorkroomApp.swift:122`).
Gating on `seed.isLaunch` (already required to reach this point in the `.task`) is exactly what stops
onboarding from being reconsidered on a ⌘N window — only the launch window's `.task` body reaches
this line at all.

Extracted as a testable static helper rather than left inline (the `.task` closure body itself isn't
unit-testable, and it's the one seam in this feature with no test at all otherwise):

```swift
extension RootWindow {
  static func shouldOpenOnboarding(seed: WindowSeed, hasCompleted: Bool, projectsEmpty: Bool) -> Bool {
    seed.isLaunch && OnboardingGate.shouldShow(hasCompleted: hasCompleted, projectsEmpty: projectsEmpty)
  }
}
```

The `.task` body calls this instead of duplicating the `seed.isLaunch &&` check.

### 4. UI-test fixture support — `Core/UITestFixture.swift`

- Add `static var onboardingOverride: Bool?` reading a plain string launch arg
  (`-WorkroomUITestOnboarding show|hide`) via the existing `text(_:)` helper — independent of
  `isActive`, like `forceWhatsNew`, so it also covers the non-fixture bootstrap path used by
  `WorkroomWorkflowUITests.testAppLaunchesWithChrome`. (Note: this is a separate string-typed flag
  read directly by application code, not a `Defaults`-typed bool read from a bare launch arg — so it
  does not hit the argument-domain-shadowing gotcha that a naive `-hasCompletedOnboarding 1` arg
  would.)
- In `applyFixtureDefaults(active:)`, pin `Defaults[.hasCompletedOnboarding] = true` alongside the
  existing `sidebarWidth`/`diffViewMode`/`themeFamily` determinism pins — otherwise a machine with a
  clean Dev Defaults domain and `-WorkroomUITestNoProjects 1` (used by e.g.
  `NewWorkroomDialogUITests`) would unexpectedly pop the wizard over an unrelated test.
- Fix `WorkroomWorkflowUITests.swift`'s `testAppLaunchesWithChrome` launch args to include
  `-WorkroomUITestOnboarding hide` (it runs with `fixture: false` against real config/Defaults, so
  the fixture pin above doesn't cover it).
- New `WorkroomAppUITests/OnboardingUITests.swift`: launches with `-WorkroomUITestFixture 1
  -WorkroomUITestNoProjects 1 -WorkroomUITestOnboarding show -ApplePersistenceIgnoreState YES`;
  asserts the window (accessibility id `onboarding.window`) appears, walks Next → Next → Cancel
  (skip) → Get Started, asserts it closes. A second test drives the real Add Project button and
  asserts auto-advance to Done.
- Same file, two relaunch tests covering the actual acceptance criterion (persistence), exercising
  the REAL gate rather than the override. **Run in non-fixture mode** (`fixture: false`, like
  `testAppLaunchesWithChrome`), not `-WorkroomUITestFixture 1` — caught by the outside-voice pass:
  `applyFixtureDefaults` only runs at all when fixture mode is active (`guard active else { return }`),
  and `-WorkroomUITestNoProjects` only has an effect through `AppStore.loadFixture()`, which is also
  fixture-mode-only — so fixture mode and "real, unpinned onboarding flag" are mutually exclusive as
  written, and the `hasCompletedOnboarding` pin added above would defeat these tests entirely if they
  ran in fixture mode. Instead: launch against a genuinely fresh, isolated config/Defaults domain
  (zero projects because nothing's registered there, not because of the `NoProjects` fixture flag) —
  same fixture-Defaults-domain-across-two-launches shape as the existing issue #46 session-restore
  relaunch tests, just without `-WorkroomUITestFixture 1` in the args. (1) launch, close the wizard
  early (⌘W, before Done), terminate, relaunch with the same args, assert the window reopens; (2) same
  setup, but walk to Done first, terminate, relaunch, assert it does NOT reopen.
- Known accepted gap, tracked in TODOS.md rather than tested now: `handleAdd`'s failure branch (add
  fails mid-wizard → step stays up, no flag set) has no test at any level — reliably forcing a
  CLI-level failure (e.g. a chmod'd-unwritable path) in XCUITest risks CI flakiness under sandboxing,
  and `AddProjectSheetModel.isValid` already disables Add for the common (malformed-path) failure
  case, so the residual risk is low.

### 5. Unit tests — new `WorkroomAppTests/OnboardingGateTests.swift`

Pure calls to `OnboardingGate.shouldShow(hasCompleted:projectsEmpty:override:)` (mirrors
`AddProjectSheetModelTests`): all 4 `(hasCompleted, projectsEmpty)` combinations — including
`(true, false)` — plus `override` forcing true/false regardless of the other params. Also covers
`RootWindow.shouldOpenOnboarding(seed:hasCompleted:projectsEmpty:)` with `WindowSeed.launch` vs
`.restoring(key:)` fixtures, asserting a non-launch seed never opens onboarding regardless of the
other two params.

### 6. `AppStoreAddProjectTests.swift` — cover the new `Result` return contract

`AppStore.addProject` changes from `Void` to `@discardableResult ... -> Result<Void, Error>` (see
design decisions — upgraded from a bare `Bool` so the wizard can show the actual error inline instead
of relying on the possibly-hidden main-window alert). The existing file covers side effects
(selection, reload) but never asserted the return value, which the wizard's `handleAdd` now depends
on. Add two assertions: a successful add returns `.success`; a CLI-level failure (invalid/unwritable
path) returns `.failure` carrying the same error `present(error)` already displays.

## Verification

1. `make cli-lint`/`make app-lint` and `make app-format` on touched files.
2. `make app-test` (unit) — `OnboardingGateTests` plus full regression.
3. `make app-generate && xcodebuild ... -only-testing:WorkroomAppUITests/OnboardingUITests` (scoped,
   per the memory on never running the full UI suite) — verify the wizard's UI test, plus a scoped
   rerun of `NewWorkroomDialogUITests`/`WorkroomWorkflowUITests` to confirm the fixture pin/launch-arg
   fix actually prevents the regression it targets.
4. Manual end-to-end, with **two** isolation layers (config is $HOME-scoped; Defaults is not):
   ```bash
   export HOME="$(mktemp -d)"
   defaults delete com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev onboarding.hasCompleted 2>/dev/null
   make app-run
   ```
   Verify: wizard opens over the empty main window on first launch; Next/Next walks Welcome → Tour;
   on Add Project, either add a real project (auto-advances to Done, main sidebar shows it selected)
   or Skip (also advances to Done); Get Started closes the wizard; relaunching does not reopen it.
   Then repeat, closing the wizard early (⌘W before reaching Done) and confirm it *does* reopen next
   launch.
5. **No-regression check for existing users** — with `hasCompletedOnboarding` already `true` (or any
   project already registered), confirm launch opens exactly one main window, no onboarding window,
   and the existing session-restore fan-out (`ProjectStore.shared.pendingSessionKeys()`) still
   reopens siblings unchanged.
6. **Window chrome, manual-only** (no automated test — see design decisions): drag the wizard
   window's edges and confirm it does NOT resize past its fixed content size
   (`.windowResizability(.contentSize)`); with `NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows` enabled in System Settings,
   quit with the wizard open and relaunch, confirming macOS does not independently reopen it
   (`isRestorable = false`) outside of `OnboardingGate`'s own check. Also confirm "Welcome to
   Workroom" disappears from the Window menu once `hasCompletedOnboarding` is `true`, and that
   `openWindow(id: OnboardingWindow.sceneID)` still works programmatically pre-completion despite
   `.commandsRemoved()` only applying post-completion.
7. **Lightweight accessibility/keyboard pass** (issue #151's only qualitative bar is "great looking,"
   which this eng review can't verify structurally — see design decisions): Tab/Shift-Tab through all
   four steps reaches every interactive control in a sensible order; Return activates the focused
   default button (Next/Add Project/Get Started) on each step; every icon-only element (the folder
   glyph, step dots) has a VoiceOver label or is `accessibilityHidden` where purely decorative,
   matching `AddProjectSheet`'s existing pattern (`accessibilityHidden(true)` on its icon).

## NOT in scope

- **Single-sheet presentation** (welcome sheet over `RootWindow`, no wizard) — considered and rejected
  by explicit user choice early in this review's planning, in favor of the 4-step wizard.
- **Sheet-over-`RootWindow` for the wizard itself** (vs. a dedicated `Window` scene) — also explicitly
  rejected by the user; the dedicated-window tradeoffs (aux-window carve-outs, Window-menu handling,
  resizability) are the direct cost of that choice.
- **`handleAdd`'s failure-path automated test** — deferred to `TODOS.md` (see Files touched). CI
  flakiness risk from a filesystem-permission trick outweighs the value for a narrow, already
  client-side-mitigated failure case.
- **Install-vs-upgrade migration detection** for the existing-user-zero-projects edge case — accepted
  as a one-time, self-correcting cosmetic caveat (see design decisions) rather than building detection
  machinery for a rare, harmless case.
- **Full `/plan-design-review` visual audit** — deferred; reviewing a text plan is a weaker signal for
  "great looking" than reviewing the actual built UI. A lightweight accessibility/keyboard pass
  substitutes in this review (Verification item 7); a full visual pass can run once a build exists.
- **Localization of the wizard's copy** — no i18n infrastructure was found anywhere else in the app
  during this review's research, so English-only copy matches the existing baseline; not a deliberate
  omission specific to this feature.
- **Onboarding funnel analytics/telemetry** (e.g. which step users drop off at) — not part of the
  issue's ask, and no telemetry system was found in the app to hook into.

## What already exists

- `ProjectSidebar`'s `ContentUnavailableView` empty-project state (`Views/ProjectSidebar.swift:96-110`)
  — reused as-is, untouched, as the fallback for anyone who skips or dismisses the wizard early.
- `AddProjectSheetModel` (`Views/AddProjectSheet.swift:16-54`) — reused directly for the wizard's
  Add-Project step validation/normalization; not rebuilt.
- `AppStore.addProject` (`Core/AppStore.swift:2983-2999`) — reused and extended (`Result`-returning)
  rather than forked; existing callers (the sidebar's own Add Project flow) unaffected.
- `ThemeService.shared`/`ThemeTokens` — reused directly for the wizard's visual language, the same
  pattern `WhatsNewSheet`/`SettingsView` already use.

  the visual template for the wizard's own step headers.

## Diagrams

Wizard step state machine (should also land as a comment on `OnboardingStep`/`OnboardingWindow` in
the implementation, per this review's diagram-maintenance expectation):

```
                    ┌─────────┐   Next    ┌──────┐   Next    ┌─────────────┐
        launch ───► │ welcome │ ────────► │ tour │ ────────► │ addProject  │
     (gate check)   └─────────┘           └──────┘           └─────────────┘
                         ▲                    │ Back              │      │
                         └────────────────────┘                   │      │ Skip
                                                          success  │      │
                                                     (sets flag)   ▼      ▼
                                                                ┌──────────┐
                                                                │   done   │──► flag set
                                                                └──────────┘    (.onChange)
                                                                     │
                                                                Get Started
                                                                     ▼
                                                            dismissWindow(sceneID)

  Any step: ⌘W / red button closes the window without advancing — flag stays whatever it
  already was (false until `.done` is reached by any path above).
```

## Failure modes

| Codepath | Realistic failure | Tested? | Error handling? | User sees |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `OnboardingGate.shouldShow` | none — pure, deterministic | Yes (unit) | n/a | n/a |
| `shouldOpenOnboarding` / `openWindow(id:)` | `.task` re-fires, double-open attempt | Covered by `openWindow(id:)`'s documented idempotency on a `Window` scene, not a dedicated test | Idempotency IS the handling | No visible effect — not a silent failure, a silent no-op success |
| `addProject` `Result` failure | CLI-level failure (permission denied, race) | Yes at the `AppStore` unit level and the wizard's success path; the wizard's own failure-path UI is the one deferred gap (TODOS.md) | Yes — `present(error)` alert AND wizard-inline text | Visible, on two channels |
| Window-menu reopen post-completion | `.commandsRemoved()` might not fully suppress the item, or might also block `openWindow(id:)` | No — explicitly flagged "verify at implementation time" | Not yet designed beyond the sketch | Flagged as a verification step, not shipped un-checked |
| Window resizability | user drags edges expecting a resize | Manual only | `.windowResizability(.contentSize)` is the handling | Visible if broken, but unverified by CI |
| macOS Cocoa window restoration | reopens window on quit-with-open + `NSQuitAlwaysKeepsWindows` | Manual only | `isRestorable = false` is the handling | Visible if broken, but unverified by CI |

No codepath has all three of "no test AND no error handling AND silent" — **zero critical gaps.**

## Worktree parallelization strategy

Dependency table (module-level):

| Step | Modules touched | Depends on |
|---|---|---|
| `AppStore.addProject` → `Result` | Core/ | — |
| `DefaultsKeys` new key | Core/ | — |
| `UITestFixture` override + pin | Core/ | — |
| `AddProjectSheet` → extract `AddProjectFields` | Views/ | — |
| `TODOS.md` entry | (repo root) | — |
| `OnboardingWindow.swift` (new) | Views/ | `AppStore`, `AddProjectFields`, `DefaultsKeys` |
| `WorkroomApp.swift` scene wiring | (root Swift file) | `OnboardingWindow.swift` |
| `AppStoreAddProjectTests` | WorkroomAppTests/ | `AppStore.addProject` change |
| `OnboardingGateTests` | WorkroomAppTests/ | `OnboardingWindow.swift`, `WorkroomApp.swift` |
| `WorkroomWorkflowUITests` arg fix | WorkroomAppUITests/ | `UITestFixture` change |
| `OnboardingUITests` (new) | WorkroomAppUITests/ | `OnboardingWindow.swift`, `WorkroomApp.swift`, `UITestFixture` |

Lanes:
- **Lane A (parallel, independent):** `AppStore` Result change, `DefaultsKeys`, `UITestFixture`,
  `AddProjectSheet` extraction, `TODOS.md` entry — no shared files, no ordering constraint.
- **Lane B (sequential, after Lane A's `AppStore`/`AddProjectFields`/`DefaultsKeys` land):**
  `OnboardingWindow.swift` → `WorkroomApp.swift`.
- **Lane C (after Lane A's `AppStore` lands):** `AppStoreAddProjectTests` — independent of Lane B.
- **Lane D (after Lane B completes):** `OnboardingGateTests` and `OnboardingUITests` in parallel with
  each other.

**Practical recommendation:** given this is a single-developer, ~10-file feature (repo mode: solo),
worktree-per-lane parallelization is likely more coordination overhead than it saves — the
above is provided per this review's standard output, but sequential implementation (Lane A → B → C/D)
is the reasonable default here rather than spinning up separate worktrees.

3	/// The first-run onboarding wizard (issue #151).
4	///
5	/// Two groups: the override-driven walkthrough (deterministic, fast) and the persistence contract
6	/// itself — the acceptance criterion this feature exists for ("still shows next launch if closed
7	/// early; never shows again once finished"). Both run in fixture mode
8	/// (`-WorkroomUITestNoProjects 1` for a reliable zero-project state), but the persistence group
9	/// additionally passes `-WorkroomUITestOnboardingRealGate 1` so `applyFixtureDefaults` does NOT pin
10	/// `hasCompletedOnboarding` — it needs the REAL, unpinned value of that key, not the
11	/// `onboardingOverride` short-circuit the walkthrough tests use.
12	///
13	/// A genuinely isolated `HOME` (non-fixture mode) was tried first for the persistence group and
14	/// empirically doesn't work: `XCUIApplication.launchEnvironment`'s `HOME` override isn't reliably
15	/// seen by the bundled CLI subprocess a GUI-launched app spawns, so it kept reading the real
16	/// `~/.config/workroom/config.json` instead of an isolated one. `Defaults` itself is also not
17	/// isolated by a throwaway `HOME` (see `ThemePickerUITests`'s doc comment) — a `defaults` shell-out
18	/// is what actually resets `hasCompletedOnboarding` between runs.
19	final class OnboardingUITests: XCTestCase {
20	  override func setUpWithError() throws { continueAfterFailure = false }
21	
22	  private let bundleID = "com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev"
23	
24	  private func launchedApp(extraArgs: [String] = []) -> XCUIApplication {
25	    let app = XCUIApplication()
26	    app.launchArguments += ["-WorkroomUITestFixture", "1", "-WorkroomUITestNoProjects", "1"]
27	    app.launchArguments += ["-ApplePersistenceIgnoreState", "YES"]
28	    app.launchArguments += extraArgs
29	    app.launch()
30	    return app
31	  }
32	
33	  // MARK: Override-driven walkthrough
34	
35	  /// Walks Welcome → Tour → skip Add Project → Done → Get Started, forced via the override so it's
36	  /// independent of the real gate/Defaults state.
37	  func testWalkthroughSkippingAddProjectClosesTheWindow() {
38	    let app = launchedApp(extraArgs: ["-WorkroomUITestOnboarding", "show"])
39	    let window = app.windows["onboarding.window"]
40	    XCTAssertTrue(window.waitForExistence(timeout: 10), "onboarding window should open")
41	
42	    app.buttons["Next"].click()  // welcome -> tour
43	    app.buttons["Next"].click()  // tour -> addProject
44	    app.buttons["Skip"].click()  // addProject -> done
45	    XCTAssertTrue(app.buttons["Get Started"].waitForExistence(timeout: 4))
46	    app.buttons["Get Started"].click()
47	
48	    let exp = XCTNSPredicateExpectation(
49	      predicate: NSPredicate(format: "exists == false"), object: window)
50	    XCTAssertEqual(
51	      XCTWaiter().wait(for: [exp], timeout: 4), .completed, "window should close on Get Started")
52	  }
53

55	  /// success path of `OnboardingWindow.handleAdd`.
56	  func testAddingARealProjectAdvancesToDone() throws {
57	    let app = launchedApp(extraArgs: ["-WorkroomUITestOnboarding", "show"])

60

62	    app.buttons["Next"].click()  // tour -> addProject

66	    defer { try? FileManager.default.removeItem(at: projectDir) }
67

69	    XCTAssertTrue(pathField.waitForExistence(timeout: 4))
70	    app.radioButtons["Create new directory…"].click()

112	      "closing before Done should leave the wizard showing again next launch")
113	  }

116	  /// the "never shows again once finished" half of the contract.
117	  func testReachingDoneNeverReopens() throws {
118	    resetHasCompletedOnboardingDefault()
119	    defer { resetHasCompletedOnboardingDefault() }
120	
121	    let app = launchedRealGateApp()
122	    let window = app.windows["onboarding.window"]
123	    XCTAssertTrue(window.waitForExistence(timeout: 10))
124	    app.buttons["Next"].click()  // welcome -> tour
125	    app.buttons["Next"].click()  // tour -> addProject
126	    app.buttons["Skip"].click()  // addProject -> done (sets the flag on entry)
127	    XCTAssertTrue(app.buttons["Get Started"].waitForExistence(timeout: 4))
128	    app.terminate()  // closed via terminate, NOT the Get Started button — flag must already be set
129	
130	    let relaunched = launchedRealGateApp()
131	    XCTAssertTrue(relaunched.wait(for: .runningForeground, timeout: 10))
132	    XCTAssertFalse(
133	      relaunched.windows["onboarding.window"].waitForExistence(timeout: 4),
134	      "reaching Done should mark onboarding complete regardless of how the window was later closed")
135	  }

## P3 — Tests and tooling

### `OnboardingUITests.testAddingARealProjectAdvancesToDone` leaks into the real CLI config (macapp) — filed 2026-08-19, issue #151

**What:** The test drives the onboarding wizard's real Add Project step, which calls the actual
bundled CLI (`AppStore.addProject` has no fixture-mode guard, only the initial project-list load
does) — registering a temp directory as a real project in the developer's actual
`~/.config/workroom/config.json`. The temp directory itself is cleaned up; the config entry is not,
so a dangling reference (pointing at an already-deleted directory) accumulates on every test run.

**Why not fixed now:** tried cleaning it up by reading/rewriting the JSON directly from the test
process — fails empirically, because the UI test runner process is itself sandboxed/containerized.
Even `ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["HOME"]` resolves to

**Built:** `DefaultsKeys.hasCompletedOnboarding`, `AppStore.addProject` upgraded to `Result<Void, Error>`, `AddProjectSheet` split into a shared `AddProjectFields` view, the new `OnboardingWindow.swift` (4-step wizard: Welcome → Tour → Add Project → Done, with lifted form state, in-flight guard, inline error display, completion set on entering Done), a `Window` scene wired in `WorkroomApp.swift` with `.windowResizability(.contentSize)` and `isRestorable = false`, plus the UI-test fixture support (`onboardingOverride`, `onboardingSeed`, `onboardingRealGate`) and new/updated tests.

## P3 — Tests and tooling

### `OnboardingUITests.testAddingARealProjectAdvancesToDone` leaks into the real CLI config (macapp) — filed 2026-08-19, issue #151

**What:** The test drives the onboarding wizard's real Add Project step, which calls the actual
bundled CLI (`AppStore.addProject` has no fixture-mode guard, only the initial project-list load
does) — registering a temp directory as a real project in the developer's actual
`~/.config/workroom/config.json`. The temp directory itself is cleaned up; the config entry is not,
so a dangling reference (pointing at an already-deleted directory) accumulates on every test run.

**Why not fixed now:** tried cleaning it up by reading/rewriting the JSON directly from the test
process — fails empirically, because the UI test runner process is itself sandboxed/containerized.
Even `ProcessInfo.processInfo.environment["HOME"]` resolves to
`~/Library/Containers/com.developwithstyle.workroom.uitests.xctrunner/Data` from inside it, not the
real home the (unsandboxed) app-under-test uses, so the test process can't reach the real config
file at all — an OS-level sandbox restriction, not a coding bug. No other existing UI test in this
suite clicks through the real Add Project flow, so this is newly-discovered territory, not a
regression.

**How to start:** either (a) drive the app's OWN delete-project affordance (which runs unsandboxed)
from within the test, right before `app.terminate()`, or (b) disable the `WorkroomAppUITests`
target's implicit sandboxing (its `XCTRunner` host may default to sandboxed; check `project.yml`
and the generated scheme) so the test process itself can read/write the real config for cleanup.

**Depends on:** nothing blocking.

**Priority:** P3 — cosmetic accumulation of dead config entries, not a functional bug; manually
clear stray `workroom-onboarding-uitest-*` keys from `~/.config/workroom/config.json` periodically
until fixed.

### Onboarding wizard's failed-add step has no test coverage (macapp) — filed 2026-08-19, issue #151

**What:** `OnboardingWindow.handleAdd`'s failure branch (a CLI-level `addProject` failure leaves the
Add Project step up, no `hasCompletedOnboarding` flag set, so the user can retry) has zero test
coverage at any level — unit or UI.

**Why not fixed now:** `AddProjectSheetModel.isValid` already disables Add for the common failure
case (malformed path), so this only fires for a genuine CLI-level failure (permission denied, a
race). Forcing that reliably in an XCUITest needs a filesystem trick (e.g. a chmod'd-unwritable temp
dir) that can behave differently under CI sandboxing/root, trading real coverage for CI flakiness.
Flagged during `/plan-eng-review` of issue #151's onboarding wizard plan; accepted as a deferred gap
rather than a blocking test.

## P3 — Tests and tooling

### Onboarding wizard's failed-add step has no test coverage (macapp) — filed 2026-08-19, issue #151

**What:** `OnboardingWindow.handleAdd`'s failure branch (a CLI-level `addProject` failure leaves the
Add Project step up, no `hasCompletedOnboarding` flag set, so the user can retry) has zero test
coverage at any level — unit or UI.

**Why not fixed now:** `AddProjectSheetModel.isValid` already disables Add for the common failure
case (malformed path), so this only fires for a genuine CLI-level failure (permission denied, a
race). Forcing that reliably in an XCUITest needs a filesystem trick (e.g. a chmod'd-unwritable temp
dir) that can behave differently under CI sandboxing/root, trading real coverage for CI flakiness —
and `AppStore.addProject`'s fixture-mode branch (added after this was filed, to stop UI tests from
touching the real `~/.config/workroom/config.json`) always simulates success, so it can no longer
even reach a failure via fixture mode at all; only a real (non-fixture) run or an injectable
`WorkroomCLIProtocol` fake could exercise this now. Flagged during `/plan-eng-review` of issue #151's
onboarding wizard plan; accepted as a deferred gap rather than a blocking test.

how does this all work for a branch new user? Can I try it?

Yes — launch it with a throwaway config + reset onboarding flag, so it thinks it's a brand-new install without touching your real projects:

```bash
export HOME="$(mktemp -d)"
defaults delete com.developwithstyle.workroom.dev onboarding.hasCompleted 2>/dev/null
make app-run
```

Type `!` before that to run it directly in this session, or paste it into your own terminal.

What this does: isolates `~/.config/workroom` to an empty temp dir (so `projects.isEmpty` is genuinely true, without touching your real config) and clears the persisted `hasCompletedOnboarding` flag (it's not `$HOME`-isolated, so it needs its own reset). `make app-run` then builds and launches "Workroom Dev" — a separate identity from your installed release build, safe to relaunch repeatedly.

Walk Welcome → Tour → either add a real project (it'll register into that throwaway config, not your real one) or Skip → Done → Get Started. Quit and rerun the same three lines to see it fresh again; if you close the wizard early (⌘W before Done) instead, rerunning `make app-run` alone (same isolated `$HOME` persists for your shell session) will show it reopening rather than staying dismissed.

content.text:
Fixed. The `orderOut(nil)` hack didn't work — SwiftUI's own `WindowGroup` launch machinery kept re-asserting the window's visibility after that callback ran. Switched to `.defaultLaunchBehavior`, the actual Apple API for this: the main window is `.suppressed` at launch whenever onboarding might be needed, and the onboarding window is `.presented` instead. Since suppressing the main window means nobody bootstraps the project list anymore, `OnboardingWindow` now does that check itself (a throwaway `AppStore` probe) and corrects course — opening the real main window and closing itself — if it turns out an existing user already has projects. Its close-notification handler (from the earlier work) now also opens a fresh main window if none exists yet, not just fronts an existing one.

Verified manually (screenshot + accessibility clicks, since XCUITest's automation subsystem is currently wedged — see below): at launch, only "Welcome to Workroom" opens, no main window behind it; closing the wizard early then opens the main window automatically. Unit tests (`OnboardingGateTests`, `AppStoreAddProjectTests`) all pass; build and lint are clean.

One thing on your screen needs your attention: there's a pending **"XCTest is trying to Enable UI Automation"** system dialog asking for Touch ID/password — I left it alone since it needs your credentials. That's very likely also why the automated `OnboardingUITests` UI-test run kept timing out ("enabling automation mode") — worth answering it, then I can rerun the full automated suite to double-check nothing regressed.

content.text: Right — `showInspector` is a single global, persisted `Defaults` key shared across every window. Toggling it off when one window has nothing selected would incorrectly hide the inspector in every other window too, and persist across relaunches. The correct fix is a view-layer gate: only render it when both the user's toggle is on *and* something's actually selected — no shared state touched, no cross-window effect.

Fix stands as implemented: `RootView.swift`'s `splitView` gates `InspectorColumn`/`ActivityBar` rail on `inspectorVisible = showInspector && store.selectedTarget != nil`, a view-layer-only condition — doesn't touch the shared `Defaults[.showInspector]` key, so other windows' inspector state is untouched. When something IS selected, `inspectorVisible == showInspector` exactly as before (no regression risk there — didn't need flaky coord-click UI automation to prove it, the logic is a straight AND against unchanged existing behavior).

  +### Onboarding wizard's failed-add step has no test coverage (macapp) — filed 2026-08-19, issue #151
  +
  +**What:** `OnboardingWindow.handleAdd`'s failure branch (a CLI-level `addProject` failure leaves the
  +Add Project step up, no `hasCompletedOnboarding` flag set, so the user can retry) has zero test
  +coverage at any level — unit or UI.
  +
  +**Why not fixed now:** `AddProjectSheetModel.isValid` already disables Add for the common failure
  +case (malformed path), so this only fires for a genuine CLI-level failure (permission denied, a
  +race). Forcing that reliably in an XCUITest needs a filesystem trick (e.g. a chmod'd-unwritable temp
  +dir) that can behave differently under CI sandboxing/root, trading real coverage for CI flakiness —
  +and `AppStore.addProject`'s fixture-mode branch (added after this was filed, to stop UI tests from
  +touching the real `~/.config/workroom/config.json`) always simulates success, so it can no longer
  +even reach a failure via fixture mode at all; only a real (non-fixture) run or an injectable
  +`WorkroomCLIProtocol` fake could exercise this now. Flagged during `/plan-eng-review` of issue #151's
  +onboarding wizard plan; accepted as a deferred gap rather than a blocking test.
  +
  +**How to start:** a UI test that creates a temp dir, `chmod`s it unwritable, points the wizard's Add
  +Project step at a path under it in create mode, and asserts the step stays up with no flag set. If
  +CI sandboxing makes the permission trick unreliable, an alternative is injecting a fake
  +`WorkroomCLIProtocol` that fails deterministically — but that requires the onboarding window to take
  +an injectable store/CLI, which it currently doesn't (see the plan for issue #151).
